entities.name: Muhammad ibn Maslamah
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Muhammad ibn Maslamah al-Ansari was a companion of the Islamic prophet Muhammad and a prominent military commander in the early Muslim community. He fought in nearly all major battles of Muhammad’s time, including Badr, Uhud, the Trench, and Khaybar, and was entrusted with special missions such as the assassination of Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf.

Born around 590 CE in Mecca, Arabia, Muhammad ibn Maslamah joined Muhammad's movement in 613 CE and became a key figure in the conquest of Medina. He served under Caliph Umar, investigating governors and participating in the Expedition of Tabuk as deputy governor.

Under Caliph Umar's leadership, he also acted as personal inspector, overseeing the governance of provinces and cities. His military campaigns were marked by strategic victories, including the Battle of Khaybar in 629 CE, where Muslim forces defeated a Jewish tribe in modern-day Saudi Arabia.

Muhammad ibn Maslamah played a significant role in shaping the early Islamic state, contributing to its expansion and growth through his military prowess and administrative acumen. His legacy as a prominent military commander and leader of the Muslim community has endured for centuries.

One of Muhammad's most notable quotes is attributed to him: 'The strongest believer is he who remains calm in the face of calamity.'
